name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis; BRIEF ratifies the /spec:mocks approved set) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.67.0 — look-stop block made copyable and navigable (direct fix, core § Incident Policy): the design stage's Step 5 prints the catalog command in a fenced code block with blank lines around it, one 🆕 line per BOUND STORY as the sidebar path `<title> / <story name>` resolved from the coverage-ledger claim's story ids through the stories file (never a component name — the 2026-09-03 field host files every story under one title with localized story names, so a search for the export name finds nothing), one ℹ️ line per component changed without a new story pointing at the story that shows it, and a fixed ↻ `Storybook already running? restart it so the sidebar re-indexes.` line. Before: the command was a bare indented line jammed against the 🆕 lines, and the 🆕 lines were component export names. Shared § Design Atlas `Look stops are never questions` now defines the fenced command, viewer-native 🆕 lines (story path for catalogs, served path for mocks) and the ↻ line for every look stop; tests/design-look-handoff.test.js re-pinned. 7.66.0 — `Depends on:` accepts a brief id with a trailing note (direct fix, core § Incident Policy): briefs spell dependencies as `16 (the review driver this brief mirrors)`; the item-wise parser rejected the item, so briefs 18, 19 and 23 silently carried no dependencies while status printed four remediation paragraphs for the tool's own strictness. spec-status.js now reads `NN`, `NN-name` or `brief NN` with one trailing parenthetical (commas inside it never split the item; header line breaks collapse); prose that is not an id still rejects and still surfaces as unparsed-dependency. Brief 24 (status-and-queue-diet) is staged for the shape that let this happen. tests/spec-status.test.js. 7.65.0 — replay-harness gaps surfaced by the first recorded replay miss (rp_0260cad37161, direct fix, core § Incident Policy): (1) `--setup --overlay` now materializes `.claude/agent-memory/` rows — worker notes are a build surface, not a review record — while the ledger, evidence, worktrees and rules under `.claude/` stay withheld; before, a host gate that sweeps those notes reddened the scratch tree on every replay for an edit the build had already made. (2) `--pick-class` skips the ids a host declares in `.claude/spec.config.json` → `replay.inapplicableClasses` (a class whose corpus section says "does not apply — pick another"), prints them as `skipped=`, refuses an id the corpus does not carry (exit 2, naming the valid ids) and refuses a list that rules out every class; this repo declares `server-code-in-client-bundle`. (3) The boundary-shift miss itself earns no guard: Incident Policy needs a third recurrence and the count is 1 — the ledger row is the record, a second miss of the class reopens the question. replay.md step 3 and Rules § Blindness, replay-corpus.md, tests/replay/replay.test.js.
